contract: resolveNpmCli(env, options) — ADR-001 of feature repo-sweep-honesty. A test that needs the real npm packer must check the IDENTITY of the tool it was handed, never the existence of a path: under pnpm, npm_execpath points at pnpm.cjs, that file exists, and an existsSync fallback therefore never fires in the one case it was written for (MEASURED 2026-09-18).
identity: A candidate is npm only if ALL THREE hold (review r1, HIGH-5 — the first and third were missing):

1. the candidate is DEREFERENCED first (realpath), because a genuine npm is normally reached through a symlink (/usr/bin/npm -> ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js) and resolving modules from /usr/bin finds nothing;

2. the nearest enclosing package.json says name == 'npm', because module resolution answers a question about a DIRECTORY — without this, any intruder dropped into a tree that contains libnpmpack passes;
3. 'libnpmpack' resolves from the dereferenced file AND the module it resolves to lives in the SAME npm installation (inside npm's own package directory, or in the node_modules that holds it).
ladder: 1. npm_execpath is used only if it passes the identity check above (the answer is the DEREFERENCED path).

2. otherwise the installed npm is looked up in the global module roots: the ambient machine roots (process.execPath layout, NODE_PATH, module.globalPaths), then npm's configured prefix, then the directories on PATH.
3. otherwise an 'npm' executable on PATH is dereferenced and identity-checked.
4. otherwise the answer is 'unavailable' carrying a reason that NAMES the tool that was not found and everywhere it was looked for.
twinGuard: packages/@dzhechkov/harness-core/test/npm-resolver-cases-twin-drift.test.ts keeps the two copies byte-identical. Two implementations exist because p-replicator PUBLISHES its tests/ directory, so it may not import from the repo root; the contract, not the code, is what is shared.

givenFields.npmExecPath: placeholder name for env.npm_execpath, or null to leave it unset
givenFields.globalRoots: 'defaultRoots' to let the resolver pick its own AMBIENT roots, or a list of placeholder names that replaces them
givenFields.env: optional map of extra environment variables; each value is a placeholder name. Env-derived roots (npm's prefix, PATH) apply even when globalRoots is overridden, because they describe the environment handed in rather than the machine
givenFields.nullArguments: optional; when true the resolver is called with explicit nulls for BOTH optional arguments instead of an env object

placeholders.npmCli: absolute path to a real npm-cli.js, located WITHOUT the resolver under test
placeholders.pnpmCli: absolute path to a real pnpm.cjs — an existing file that is NOT npm
placeholders.decoyCli: a freshly written .js file that exists and is NOT npm; the fixture that an existence check would wrongly accept
placeholders.intruderCli: a freshly written .js file that is NOT npm but sits in a tree where 'libnpmpack' DOES resolve; the fixture that a resolution-only check would wrongly accept
placeholders.npmCliSymlink: a symlink pointing at the real npm-cli.js; the fixture a resolver that does not dereference would wrongly reject
placeholders.npmPrefix: npm's install prefix, derived from `npm root -g` without the resolver under test
placeholders.npmrcHome: a directory holding a .npmrc whose `prefix=` names npmPrefix
placeholders.npmBinDir: a directory holding a symlink named 'npm' that points at the real npm-cli.js, as a bin directory on PATH does
placeholders.missingPath: an absolute path that does not exist
placeholders.emptyRoot: an existing directory holding no npm installation
placeholders.defaultRoots: the resolver's own ambient global-root list, whatever it is on this machine

cases.why: the happy path the whole ladder exists to preserve: a real npm hand-off is honoured
the measured defect: pnpm.cjs exists, so an existence check accepts it and the caller then loads pnpm as if it were npm
machine-independent proof that IDENTITY is checked and not EXISTENCE; this file always exists
review r1 HIGH-5: resolving libnpmpack proves something about the DIRECTORY, not about the file; without the enclosing-package check any file dropped beside a node_modules/libnpmpack passed as npm
review r1 HIGH-5, the other half: a genuine npm is normally reached through a symlink, and resolving from the symlink's own directory finds nothing — the real npm was being rejected
a stale hand-off must fall through the ladder rather than crash the caller
direct runs (npx vitest run / node --test) set no npm_execpath at all
review r1 HIGH-5: an npm installed under an unrelated prefix is invisible to process.execPath and to globalPaths, and was reported absent on a machine that has it
the same question `npm config get prefix` answers, read from npm's own user config instead of by spawning npm (spawning the tool you are looking for is circular)
review r1 HIGH-5: the fallback ignored PATH, yet a bin directory on PATH is how the user runs npm at all; the entry there is a symlink, so this also proves the dereferencing

review r1 LOW-7: a default parameter fires only on undefined, so the TypeScript twin threw on resolveNpmCli(null) while the CommonJS twin fell back to process.env — two twins that disagree on a value a caller can pass are not twins
FR-4: absence is reported with a NAMED reason, never as a pass and never as a crash
